employees.name: Ollie Mckinlay
employees.summary: Ollie is carrying 43 open items across six accounts on almost no message volume: one message in seven days on Lauren Blake, nothing on Vale since Aug 20, nothing on Amber Haze since Aug 18, nothing on Vicky since Aug 17, and two questions to Kaitlynn on Aug 27 after nine days of silence. On four of those accounts the client did their half and got nothing back — Vale uploaded the $2,000 John custom with its $200 rush fee on Aug 22 and six days later nobody has confirmed the fan received it; Amber committed three customs for Aug 23 and was never checked on; Lauren Blake's livestream, which Ollie built a subscriber poll for, was never rebooked and never happened; Alanna's Aug 17 and Aug 24 pinned drops both passed with zero coverage. The one bright spot is real: his Aug 27 funnel analysis on Alanna (32-million-view reel producing almost no free-page traffic) is the first strategic thinking that account has had in 25 days. Roughly $5,000 of fan money is sitting undelivered under his name across Vale and Vicky, with chargeback exposure on both.

clients.notes: The Aug 17 and Aug 24 pinned scene drops both passed with zero in-chat coverage (11 and 4 days overdue) and Aug 29 has never been mentioned by anyone since she pinned it on 8/3.

Wesley's anniversary sends — the Aug 11 flowers video and the Aug 14 five-part custom/sexting session — are 17 and 14 days past with no confirmation anywhere in the chat, and he has not posted since Aug 18.
Her Aug 19 never-sold content drop is 21 days from the ask and 9 days past the date with zero mentions; the string 'aug 19' appears once in the entire chat, in her own message.

One message in seven days ('Okay perfect thank you', Aug 22) while holding the written boundary confirmation (26 days), the whale-reactivation report (21 days) and the CodyBeebs proof screenshot (10 days).
Silent 8 days on the account with five fan-trust incidents in 35 days; the Aug 11 private-live resale is 16 days past his only remedy, a verbal word to one PPV specialist, with nothing written down.
His last words were 'Yes all solved' on Aug 17; she terminated 18 hours later and her one concrete request — disconnect @vickycutiee and mermaidua from ALTR's Infloww — is 10 days unanswered.

strengths: Produced the first genuinely strategic observation on Alanna in 25 days (Aug 27): a reel doing 32 million views against 'extremely minimal' free-page traffic, with a hypothesis that subs are going straight to VIP on the 30-day FTL.
Surfaced a $2,000 custom on Vale that fan John had paid for in May and that the client had never been told about (Aug 18), and converted the delay into an extra $200 for ASAP delivery.
coaching_flags: Near-zero message volume on 5 of 6 accounts while owning 43 open items: 1 message in 7 days on Lauren Blake (5 items he owns), nothing on Vale since Aug 20 (8 overdue), nothing on Amber Haze since Aug 18 (4 items), nothing on Vicky since Aug 17, 2 questions on Kaitlynn after 9 days silent.

When he does break silence it is to ask the client for something rather than report to them: Kaitlynn 'where have you been bringing subs in these last few days?' after 21 days with no performance update; Vale asked for more wall posts and better set variety on Aug 18 while the sexting-set template he promised on Jul 28 is 31 days undelivered; Amber asked for 3 customs on Aug 18 and never followed up.

Client content rules get a verbal 'will get this sorted' and are never written down — Lauren Blake's topless/no-face/diamond-pricing rule (26 days, already violated once in production), Amber Haze's Jul 14 boundary brief (45 days, 3 breaches), Vale's no-reselling-private-lives rule (16 days) and her girl-girl vault purge (26 days unconfirmed). Four rules, four accounts, zero artefacts.

Paid fan orders age with no delivery date across two accounts: Vale carries Ryan's $600 call (83 days), John's $1,800 videocall (119 days) and Tyler's $700 custom (145 days); Vicky leaves behind Jake's $700 call (56 days) and a $1,000 custom that can no longer be filmed. Roughly $5k of fan money, and chargebacks are the explicit fear on both accounts.

Work the client delivers goes unacknowledged: Vale's Aug 22 feed posts and $2,200 custom (6 days, no reply), Kaitlynn's Aug 19 drop (21 days, no mention), Alanna's Aug 17 and Aug 24 pinned scenes (no coverage either time). Three clients delivering into an empty room.

employees.name: Vivek
employees.summary: Vivek was introduced to clients as the named 'Meta Support Rep' on six accounts and has never sent a single message on four of them — Chey Mai (30 days), Liza Kovalenko (30 days), Mila (30 days) — and has sent exactly 1 message in 754 on Haileigh Cox, whose shadowban ask is 30 days old. Where he is active he goes silent mid-thread, usually straight after asking for credentials: on Lilia he asked for a login code at 12:47 on Aug 24, she answered inside 60 seconds, and he has not been seen in the four days since despite 6 client chases and 6 internal @-pings; on Paige his last word is 'Okay' on Aug 27 with the fourth IG lockout in 30 days still open. He is also the largest security exposure in the book: five plaintext credential posts in Paige's group chat in 30 days (she is now guessing between two passwords), two Facebook passwords plus a live 2FA code sitting 21 days in Lauryn's chat, and passwords and a login code in Sarah's. The oldest platform failures in the agency are all his and none moved: Lauryn's Facebook 'not recommended' at 335 days (21 into his escalation, 12 with full account access, total output 'Just tested something' and 'Still in review'), and Sarah's 530k main IG suspended 19 days with 18 days of no update. He did restore Amber Haze's posting access on Aug 19 and resolved Paige's Aug 21 lockout in 7 minutes, so the capability is there when he engages.

Accepted the barbarasilva.vip domain review with 'Yeah will do' on Aug 24 — the strongest root-cause lead anyone has produced on her IG problem, and it came from the client — and has sent nothing in the 4 days since.

Introduced Jul 29 as the Meta Support Rep on the one service topic she ever raised unprompted; 30 days later he has never posted a single message and the Copyright Ban Protection setup was never actioned.

She asked about a suspected shadowban within 2 minutes of his introduction on 7/29, he replied 'Sure share login', and there have been zero messages from either side in the 30 days since — his lifetime total on this account is 1 message out of 754.

The Facebook 'not recommended' flag is 335 days old and 21 days into his escalation; with full account access since Aug 16 his entire seven-day output was 'Just tested something' and 'Still in review', and he never answered her direct 'Did it work!????'.
Ten days on the TikTok shadowban; she diagnosed it herself on Aug 22 and cannot post at all, and he vanished after asking for a login code she supplied in under a minute on Aug 24.
Thirty days in the chat as the named escalation path for her stated #1 concern (IG flagging, open 322 days) with zero messages ever sent.
Thirty days, zero messages, on a client whose Instagram had already been suspended twice before he was announced to her.

Fourth IG lockout in 30 days and the first to cross a week boundary unresolved — 97 minutes to first reply on Aug 26, an overnight stall, a chatter having to bump him publicly, then 'Send logins' producing a fifth plaintext credential post in which the client is guessing between two passwords.
Her main @sarah.h44 (~530k) has been suspended 19 days and his last message of any kind on this account was 21:20 on Aug 9 — 18 days of silence on her single stated priority.
Twenty days since 'Wait i will explain' on the Instagram profile-views collapse from 20M to 4M; she has now gone two consecutive weeks without raising IG or Facebook at all.
Her Aug 3 referral of a creator interested in management was tagged onward and never came back to her — 25 days of silence toward a client who has generated $5,720 of referral credit.

strengths: Restored Amber Haze's Instagram posting access on Aug 19 after her Aug 14 report — she is back on the grid and that half of the problem is genuinely closed.
Resolved Paige's Aug 21 lockout in 7 minutes, the only interaction on that account she has ever praised twice.
On Lauryn he replied within 12 hours of her Aug 25 chase and is evidently still actively testing the Facebook appeal rather than having abandoned it.
coaching_flags: Announced to clients as 'Meta Support Rep' and then never speaks: zero messages ever on Chey Mai (30 days), Liza Kovalenko (30 days) and Mila (30 days), and 1 message in 754 on Haileigh Cox (30 days on her shadowban). Four accounts were sold a named escalation path that has never said a word.

Goes silent mid-thread immediately after requesting credentials: Lilia (asked for a login code Aug 24 12:47, she answered in 60 seconds, 4 days silent, 6 client chases and 6 internal @-pings), Paige (last word 'Okay' Aug 27, issue still open), Sarah (silent 18 days since 'okay no problem thanks' on Aug 9), Sarah Lloyd (20 days since 'Wait i will explain').

Credentials are being collected in client group chats and never rotated: 5 plaintext password posts on Paige in 30 days across 11 messages (she now cannot name her own password), 2 Facebook passwords plus a phone number and a live SMS 2FA code sitting 21 days in Lauryn's chat, passwords and a login code in Sarah's on Aug 7 and Aug 9, TikTok login in Lilia's on Aug 18. He wrote 'Send login in dm' on Paige's chat on Aug 13 and has broken his own rule three times since.

Two-to-four word answers that do not answer the question, on four accounts: 'Normally' and 'Yeah you can post' to Amber Haze's third ask about clearing IG warnings (14 days), 'Still in review' to Lauryn's 'Did it work!????' on a 335-day flag, 'Yes on it' to Lilia's shadowban (10 days), 'Hell nah' to Paige after a wrong-account approval request (14 days unexplained).

The agency's longest-running platform failures are all his and all static this week: Lauryn's Facebook 335 days, Sarah's 530k main IG 19 days suspended with 18 days of no update, Sarah's two backup accounts 22 days blocked on a single screenshot request nobody has repeated in 20 days, Haileigh's shadowban 30 days with zero chases in either direction.

employees.name: Stephski
employees.summary: Stephski touched 15 of 19 accounts this week and is still the only ALTR function that reliably follows up on itself — her Aug 26 nudges recovered stalled invoices on Paige, Lauryn and Chey Mai the same day, she cleared Lilia's ~$1,692 consolidated balance to $0 with zero chasing, and she confirmed Sarah Lloyd's payment after two bounced wires. The problem is the account-number change she put inside the Aug 15 invoice message. It has now produced bounced or failed wires on three accounts — Liza Kovalenko ($2,433 of $7,433 unaccounted, the client diagnosing the bounce herself), Lauren Blake (two rejections, invoice 2 unpaid at 13 days) and Sarah Lloyd (two bounces, four days late, resolved only by falling back to the old 4709 account) — and unconfirmed receipts on five more (Vale 11 days, Mila 11 and 17, Paige 24, Haileigh 8, Shayna 2). Chases are landing 11 days late as a pattern (Alanna, Chey Mai, Lauryn, Paige) and four one-line client questions are unanswered: Chey Mai's PayPal ask at 46 days, Kaitlynn's cadence question at 11, Shayna's Zelle-cap question at 8 (never actually answered), Haileigh's 'which account?' at 10. Two clients are also simply not being billed — Kaitlynn has had one invoice in four weeks and Hannah's final invoice is 44 days past cadence.

clients.notes: Her four-word chase on Aug 26 — 'Hi love checking in on this' — got a client reply in 3.5 hours and surfaced that the first-ever invoice had gone 11 days unpaid; still unconfirmed at 13 days.
The $1,989 July reconciliation gap is 32 days open and her only message of the week was 'Thank!' — acknowledging a payment whose amount is stated nowhere in the chat.
Nothing outstanding, but her Aug 31 pre-invoice withdrawal reminder is now the only scheduled proactive ALTR contact on this account before Sept 1 — do not let it slip.

Acknowledged the Aug 19-20 payment on Aug 26 — six days after the money landed and with no total confirmed, against a previous cycle where she asked 'can you confirm the total you sent?' and closed it inside a minute.

Two invoices are overdue simultaneously for the first time (July 15-31 at 27 days, the combined Aug 15 bill 6 days past due); the Aug 26 chase came 11 days after the extension lapsed and went to the Invoicing topic the client has already said she does not see.

Her 8/18 question about which account to wire to is 10 days unanswered by the person who sent the invoice; the only acknowledgement of the 8/20 wire is 'Thank!' on 8/26, which confirms neither receipt nor destination.
The final 7/1-7/7 invoice is 44 days past ALTR's own cadence date, blocked on earning statements requested twice from a client who churned 53 days ago — no chases in three consecutive weeks.

No invoice for Aug 15-21 or Aug 22-28 and no reply to 'For invoicing, is it weekly or bi-weekly typically?' in 11 days; she has not posted in this group since Aug 15 and the client reported unexplained wire friction that was never diagnosed.

Two wires rejected against the changed account number and invoice 2 unpaid at 13 days; last week's recommendation to re-confirm the banking details in a standalone message was not done, and her only message all week was another chase.

Eleven days with no follow-up on the Aug 15 invoice against her usual 3-4 day nudge, then two escalations in four hours on Aug 26 — the client replied warmly inside 13 hours, but the gap is why the bill went 6 days past terms.

Best billing outcome in the book — 'Yes mam you're totaled at $0 owed now' on Aug 26, second consecutive cycle with zero chasing — but the client had reported owing $192 the day before and nobody reconciled the gap.

The client paid $7,433 on Aug 19, got six days of silence, chased, and was told only $5,000 had arrived; she then diagnosed the bounce out of ALTR's changed account herself and volunteered the sender names, and her last three messages sat 37 hours unanswered.

Two wires unreconciled — the Aug 17 payment 11 days unconfirmed against an account number changed after she was told on Jul 13 to 'just repeat to the same account', and the Jul 15-31 duplicate check 20 days past 'Will update you shortly!'.

The Aug 26 nudge worked in hours ('i already sent it babe x' plus a screenshot), but the Aug 4 wire is 24 days unconfirmed and the screenshot is unacknowledged against a bank account that changed on this exact invoice.
First missed cycle in eleven months — the Aug 1-14 invoice arrived 6 days late with no apology and was overstated; the client caught it, her third catch of an ALTR billing error in four months.

Her wire bounced twice off the third bank change in ten weeks and was flagged by the client's bank as suspicious; 'Received!' on Aug 26 closed it, four days past terms, only after reverting to the old 4709 account.

Her 8/18 question about whether the new Zelle recipient reset her $1,000/day cap went 8 days unanswered and was never actually answered; the invoice ran 4 days late and 'Hi everything is sent!' is still unacknowledged two days on.

Eleven days without confirming a payment sent to the changed account number, from a client who is 9-for-9 on time since March; Stephski has sent nothing to this chat since Aug 15 and the Sep 1 invoice is due.

The churned client asked for a final Aug 1-18 figure on Aug 17; ten days later the only follow-up is '@vallume Hi can you please finish out your last invoice' — no amount, no wallet address, no acknowledgement she had terminated. That is the last thing ALTR ever said to her.

strengths: Cleared Lilia's consolidated ~$1,692 invoice to $0 and volunteered the confirmation before being asked ('On our sheet it says you're paid up!', Aug 26) — the second consecutive cycle on that account needing zero payment reminders.

Her Aug 26 nudges recovered three stalled invoices inside a day: Paige replied 'i already sent it babe x' with a screenshot, Lauryn gave verbal confirmation within 13 hours after 11 days of silence, and Chey Mai's balance was re-opened after two weeks of nothing.

Closed the Sarah Lloyd cycle with 'Received!' on Aug 26 after two wires bounced off ALTR's own new bank account, and confirmed Sarah's payment within a day — faster than the three-day confirmation on the previous cycle.
On Alanna, a four-word chase surfaced an unpaid first invoice within 3.5 hours after 11 days of total silence — she remains the most reliable closer of her own loops on that account.
coaching_flags: The Aug 15 account-number change is now causing failed payments, not just friction: wires bounced on Liza Kovalenko ($2,433 of $7,433 still unaccounted, client diagnosed it herself), Lauren Blake (two rejections, invoice unpaid at 13 days) and Sarah Lloyd (two bounces, 4 days late, fixed only by reverting to the old 4709 account). Three clients, six weeks after 'last change I promise!'.

Receipt confirmation is not happening across the book: Vale 11 days, Mila 11 and 17 days, Paige 24 days on the Aug 4 wire plus the Aug 26 screenshot unacknowledged, Haileigh 8 days answered only with 'Thank!', Shayna 2 days after 'Hi everything is sent!', Barbara 6 days with no total. Six clients sent money to a changed account and were never told it landed.

Chases are arriving ~11 days after issue and only once: Alanna (first chase day 11), Chey Mai (11 days after the extension lapsed, now two invoices overdue), Lauryn (11 days, then 'we are multiple invoices unpaid'), Paige (11 days — she had already paid). The day-2/day-5 cadence that demonstrably works is not being run anywhere.

One-line client billing questions go unanswered for weeks: Chey Mai's PayPal question 46 days, Kaitlynn's 'weekly or bi-weekly?' 11 days, Shayna's $1,000/day Zelle-cap question 8 days and still never answered, Haileigh's 'which account do I wire to?' 10 days. All four are single-sentence answers and all four cost a payment cycle.

Invoices are being missed outright — this is unbilled revenue, not client risk: Kaitlynn has had one invoice in four weeks with Aug 15-21 (6 days late) and Aug 22-28 unissued, Hannah's final 7/1-7/7 invoice is 44 days past cadence, and Sarah's Aug 1-14 invoice broke a ~23-cycle on-time streak by arriving 6 days late and overstated.

employees.name: Fred
employees.summary: Fred is fast on apologies and slow-to-silent on instructions, and the gap is now costing money on both his accounts. On Lilia the chat team resold owned content to a high spender for the eighth time since Jun 12 — this time on the red set she had personally filed for Adam West, the named premium lead she sourced four days earlier — he apologised in 53 seconds and has said nothing about it in the five days since; his Jul 24 promise to remove the offending chatter is 35 days old and the chatter has still never been named. Her two revenue instructions of Aug 26 (share-for-shares, and repricing the 3-minute sexting sets individually with photos) were still unanswered 41 and 37 hours later despite Mayson escalating. On Shayna he sent one message in seven days, on Aug 23, and it was a request for a custom; her reply — 'Please let chatters know this' about her Aug 26 return — is four days unanswered, so the chatters are still running a month-old Africa narrative. Meanwhile the fans who paid for VIP on a full-nude promise are 17 days with no refund decision, audit or chargeback check, and the tracker he has owed since Jul 20 was finally unblocked on Aug 28 by the client signing up for Notion herself.

One message in seven days and it was an ask; the fans who paid for VIP on a full-nude promise are 17 days with no refund, substitute, audit or chargeback check, and the replacement chatter promised on 8/11 has never been named so she does not know who is on her account.

No live items, but the churn post-mortem names him: he onboarded her as sole point of contact through Jun 22 and disappeared on Jun 26 with Ollie taking over the same hour and no handover message ever sent to the client.

strengths: Acknowledged Lilia's Aug 23 mishandling complaint in 53 seconds with a straight apology and no excuses — the fastest client-facing response on that account this week.
Chased the upload status himself on Aug 26 ('is it fully uploaded'), his first proactive move on the content-organising commitment since Aug 10.
Thought ahead on Shayna on Aug 23 by asking her return date specifically so a waiting fan could be managed rather than left hanging.
coaching_flags: Fast on apologies and all-clears, slow or silent on instructions — the highest-risk category — on both accounts: Lilia's Aug 26 share-for-share notice unanswered 41 hours after a Mayson escalation and her sexting-set repricing 37 hours, her Aug 25 upload embargo acknowledged after 12h56m; Shayna's Aug 24 'Please let chatters know this' unanswered 4 days. That is 5 Mayson escalations of Fred on Lilia since Jul 23.

Chatter conduct is corrected with verbal briefings and never with a written rule or a mechanical control, and it does not hold: Lilia's reselling has recurred 8 times since Jun 12 across four team briefings, with the Jul 24 'I will take them off your account' 35 days old and the chatter unnamed; Shayna's no-free-content rule has recurred 9 times since Apr 15, the vault-notes entry promised Aug 6 is 22 days unconfirmed and the PG mass-message folder 23 days unbuilt.

Client-volunteered revenue instructions sit idle across both accounts: Lilia's Adam West red-set sale (9 days, mishandled instead of sold), her $100/min shower custom (17 days since 'will inform team'), her high-spender folder organisation (18 days), Teddi's return prep (20 days); Shayna's Aug 7 untracked-custom question (21 days) and two live custom pushes — the Aug 16 big spender and the fan 'Jim' — with no price, fan handle or due date recorded anywhere.

Tracking work gets handed back to the client: Shayna asked for a shared tracker on Jul 20 and said explicitly she did not want to sign up for a tool; 39 days later she set up Notion herself and sent her email asking for the invite. Lilia files her own content into the high-spender folder because 'let me know when it's all up and I'll organise' (Aug 10) never happened. Both clients are doing his admin.
